source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Report the recurring care issue through the appropriate process and participate in a structured review of causes, evidence-based changes, and outcome data.","B":"Identify one nurse involved in the most recent transfer and treat that individual as the sole cause without examining the recurring process problem.","C":"Ignore the pattern if no client has yet been seriously harmed because performance-improvement review should begin only after a sentinel event occurs.","D":"Create a personal transfer form and use it without informing the unit because individual undocumented workarounds are preferable to a coordinated improvement process."}}
source_row.rationale: The 2026 NCSBN test plan expects RNs to report identified client-care issues, participate in quality-improvement processes, use evidence, and evaluate the effect of improvements. Option A addresses the repeated process problem systematically. Option B prematurely assigns individual blame, Option C delays action until harm occurs, and Option D creates an uncoordinated workaround rather than improving the care system.
source_row.source_detail: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan — Management of Care, Performance Improvement (Quality Improvement), printed p.22: report identified client-care issues to appropriate personnel; participate in PI/QI processes; use research and references for improvement actions; evaluate impact on client care. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; official NCSBN/NCLEX source currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: continuity/transfer of care, collaboration, legal/regulatory scope, quality improvement, leadership and professional-practice activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: A staff nurse notices repeated omissions in medication-reconciliation information during transfers between units. Which response best supports quality improvement?
